History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 29-year-old female with no significant past medical history presents via teleconsult with a new, 1-day history of left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia; clinical impression is probable first migraine; advised NSAID trial, hydration, monitoring, and BP check.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe, left-sided throbbing headache started yesterday morning on waking; constant baseline with fluctuating intensity.
- Course: Persisted x 24 h, not previously experienced; improved slightly with lying down and paracetamol; exacerbated by light; no clear positional, cough, or strain component.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia. Denies visual disturbances, abnormal smells/tastes, nausea, vomiting, fever/chills, rhinorrhea, otalgia, skin changes, limb weakness, numbness, or tingling.
- Triggers/preceding factors: Possible work-related stress; no menstrual association (last period 1 week ago).
- Review of systems: Negative for respiratory, gastrointestinal, neurologic focal deficits, constitutional symptoms.
  
Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses, hospitalizations, or surgeries reported.

Medications:
- Microgynon oral contraceptive pill, dose/route/frequency not documented (started ~6 y ago).
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) self-administered for current headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Aspirin – causes severe nausea (“feels really sick”).

Social History:
- Lives with friends/housemates.
- Alcohol: “Normal amount,” a few drinks on weekends.
- Smoking: Denies.
- Recreational drugs: Denies.
- Employment: Working; reports recent stress.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension and migraines.
- No other familial conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals or physical findings recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.
- Advised to obtain blood pressure reading and thermometer for home temperature monitoring.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: New-onset unilateral throbbing headache, likely migraine
  - Plan:
    • Start ibuprofen or other NSAID with ongoing paracetamol as needed (ensure taken with food).  
    • Maintain adequate hydration.  
    • Minimize light exposure; rest in dark, quiet room.  
    • Monitor for red-flag features: worsening or persistent headache, fever, rash, neurological deficits, changes with posture, or visual symptoms.  
    • If any red flags or lack of improvement, seek urgent medical review or call clinic.

Issue 2: Need for baseline vitals and cardiovascular assessment
  - Plan:
    • Arrange blood pressure check (has not been measured for ~6 months).  
    • Consider routine BP monitoring given family history of hypertension and OCP use.

Issue 3: Headache prophylaxis/recurrence
  - Plan:
    • If headaches become recurrent, discuss menstrual association, triggers, and possible prophylactic therapy in follow-up.

General Plan:
  - Obtain home thermometer; monitor temperature during illness episodes.  
  - Follow-up: Patient to contact clinic if symptoms worsen, new symptoms develop, or no improvement in 1–2 days.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected: Objective vitals, neurological exam, complete medication reconciliation (doses/frequency), allergy specifics (reaction type clarified but severity unknown).  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor background dialogue but clinically adequate.
